text:
raj: heads up we're iterating on how sampling interacts with the envelope approach for billing attribution. want to surface trade-offs before RFC appendix.

sophie: quick summary of the problem: sampled traces may drop high-card billing attrs, losing attribution.

dylan: thought: keep envelope.meta always + when sampled, emit a hashed bucket for each high-card attr so we can proportionally attribute costs.

nora: hashing sounds good but legal asked whether that counts as pseudonymous data. policy-bot: please consult the data classification doc.

policy-bot: reminder: hashed identifiers are still sensitive if reversible or linkable across systems. approval required.

raj: operationally, need two behaviors: (A) preserve envelope.meta + hashed bucket on sampled traces; (B) optionally keep exact values in private deployments or billing-authorized services.

sophie: implementational detail: SDK should emit envelope.meta by default, and a separate call attachEnvelopeValues(force=true) for exact values. console flag toggles behavior per service.

dylan: sampling interplay: when trace is dropped, telemetry metrics should still increment an "attribution_inferred" counter if we resolved billing via lookup. helps reconciliation.

billing-team: can we run a sim? if we keep hashed buckets for 1% sample, how accurate are per-customer cost estimates vs full-fidelity? dylan: rough ballpark: 95% for >1000 requests/day tenants, but poor for tiny tenants.

raj: proposal for RFC appendix: - envelope v1 spec (meta, buckets, provenance) - sampling rules: preserve meta + per-attr hash buckets + sample_rate metadata - reconciliation playbook: inferred vs attributed split metrics + alert when inferred > 10% of total cost for a service.

sophie: add monitoring: a weekly job that compares billed revenue from attribution vs invoiced usage; if discrepancy > 2% create incident.

nora: compliance asks: make hashing non-deterministic across environments to avoid cross-tenant linkage between hosted and private. document that.

dylan: note on queries: hashed buckets mean we can't run exact per-tenant time-series on samples; only proportional estimates. doc that limitation in the console UI.

policy-bot: created approval ticket GOV-212 for hashing scheme review.

raj: action items: dylan -> produce sim numbers for 1%, 5%, 10% sample (due Thu). sophie -> SDK shim POC that emits meta+hash (branch by Wed). nora -> coordinate GOV-212 review. billing-team -> curate test tenants for pilot.

raj: ok, i'll fold these into the appendix and include example queries + a reconciliation alert template. thanks all.
